company_description: The Coca-Cola Company, a beverage company, manufactures and sells various nonalcoholic beverages in the United States and internationally. The company provides Trademark Coca-Cola, sparkling soft drinks and flavors; water, sports, coffee, and tea; juice, value-added dairy, and plant-based beverages; and emerging beverages. It also offers beverage concentrates and syrups, as well as fountain syrups to fountain retailers comprising restaurants and convenience stores. risks.title: Intense competition in non-alcoholic beverages
risks.summary: Coca-Cola faces increased competition from major groups (PepsiCo, Keurig Dr Pepper) and local or craft brands in carbonated drinks, water, teas, and functional beverages, putting pressure on market share, pricing, and innovation.
risks.score_rationale: Listed first in Item 1A, strong language ("intense competition", "significant competitive pressures"), stable trend, high weight as it relates to the core business.

risks.title: Dependence on key bottling partners
risks.summary: The company relies heavily on a few independent bottlers (such as Coca-Cola FEMSA, CCEP, CCHBC), whose mismanagement, financial difficulties, or operational issues could disrupt distribution and reduce product availability in key markets.
risks.score_rationale: High position in the text, concerned language ("reliance", "disruption"), stable trend, critical category for the supply chain.

risks.title: Increased regulation on health and labeling
risks.summary: Governments are imposing taxes on sugary drinks, restrictive front-of-pack labels, and advertising restrictions, particularly in Latin America, Europe, and Asia, which curbs consumption and increases compliance costs.
risks.score_rationale: Central position among risks, strong language ("increasing regulation", "taxes on sugary drinks"), rising trend, direct impact on demand and costs.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of distribution systems and customer data
risks.summary: A cyberattack could paralyze production and distribution systems or compromise sensitive consumer and partner data, as recently observed in other major food industry players.
risks.score_rationale: New risk explicitly mentioned in Item 1C, alarming language ("material disruption", "data breach"), rising trend, high operational and reputational impact.

risks.title: Pressure on traditional brands from health trends
risks.summary: Declining consumption of traditional sodas in favor of sugar-free, organic, functional, or alternative beverages (water, teas, plant-based drinks) threatens the growth of legacy brands like Coca-Cola Classic, despite innovation efforts.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the context of portfolio evolution, concerned language ("changing consumer preferences"), stable trend, structural impact on demand.

risks.title: Dependence on key suppliers for ingredients and packaging
risks.summary: The availability and cost of raw materials (sugar, sweeteners, PET, aluminum) depend on a limited number of suppliers; any supply disruption or price increase could affect margins and production continuity.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the context of disruptions, concerned language ("reliance on key suppliers"), stable trend, direct impact on production.

risks.title: Risks related to expansion into alcoholic beverages
risks.summary: Entry into the alcoholic beverage market (such as Topo Chico Hard Seltzer) exposes Coca-Cola to specific regulations, complex licensing, and reputational risks related to alcohol consumption, particularly among young people.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned as a new area, cautious language ("regulatory scrutiny", "firewalled subsidiary"), rising trend, sensitive category due to strict regulations.

ai_positioning.summary: Coca-Cola acknowledges the growing impact of AI, data analytics, and automation on the competitive digital landscape and consumer behavior. The company identifies the increasing use of AI across digital platforms as a factor transforming brand discovery and engagement. The uncertain regulatory framework for AI is identified as a potential risk for compliance costs and usage limitations.
evidence: The increasing use of data analytics, automation and artificial intelligence across digital platforms is further reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate and engage with brands.

The legal and regulatory landscape for certain new technologies, such as artificial intelligence, is uncertain and evolving, and our compliance obligations could increase our costs or limit how we may use these technologies.
